entry.idea: Cornelis Networks builds the networking hardware that connects thousands of AI chips together, so they spend less time waiting for data and more time computing.
entry.lesson: When a giant player like Nvidia locks customers into its own hardware, sell an open alternative that works with everyone else's chips.
entry.name: Cornelis Networks

growth.reason: It raised $205M, a big new round, and launched a new flagship product with a major hardware partner in the same announcement.

market.reason: Every company building large AI or supercomputing clusters worldwide needs high-speed networking between chips, a fast-growing and very large market.

tech.reason: Building an open networking fabric that beats specialized hardware like InfiniBand on speed and latency took decades of interconnect engineering that a new team could not quickly match.

entry.twist: Its new Active Compute Fabric does some of the data-moving work inside the network itself instead of on the chips, and it works with any brand of GPU, unlike Nvidia's own closed networking gear.
entry.who_pays: National laboratories, large AI and high-performance-computing centers, and hardware makers pay for Cornelis's network switches, adapters and cables.
entry.why_now: AI companies are building huge clusters of GPUs, and the network connecting those chips has become one of the biggest bottlenecks and costs in running them.

mentions.snippet: Network technology that stops GPUs wasting time waiting for data; raised $205M.
